key_insight: STEM replaces the FFN up-projection with a static, token-indexed layer-local embedding lookup while keeping the gate and down-projection dense, removing runtime routing and enabling CPU offload with asynchronous prefetch to scale parameter capacity without proportional per-token compute.
problem_solved: Solves instability, load-balancing and communication overheads of fine-grained sparsity, enabling higher parametric capacity with lower runtime routing and memory pressure.
method: Replace FFN up-projection with a static, token-indexed layer-local embedding lookup (embedding modules) to provide sparse parameter capacity.
Retain dense gating and down-projection to preserve expressivity and training stability.
Eliminate runtime routing and support CPU offload + asynchronous prefetch to reduce communication and per-token compute overhead.
impact: Enables practitioners to scale transformer capacity more cheaply and stably—more parameters for similar per-token cost—and simplifies deployment across GPU/CPU memory tiers by removing dynamic routing.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: standard FFN vs STEM highlighting embedding lookup replacing the up-projection and dense gate/down-projection
Chart: params vs per-token compute showing higher capacity at near-constant per-token cost with STEM
Pipeline diagram: GPU/CPU memory tiers with asynchronous prefetch for embedding modules
Comparison infographic: routing-based sparse methods (instability, load imbalance, comms) vs STEM (static, routing-free, offloadable)
paper_title: STEM: Scaling Transformers with Embedding Modules
paper_authors: Ranajoy Sadhukhan, Sheng Cao, Harry Dong, Changsheng Zhao, Attiano Purpura-Pontoniere
